svg.title: The Paddock family
svg.desc: Seven local-first desktop apps. Pacenotes, Debrief and Sighter above, Spotter, Dyno and Pitcrew below, Pitwall the optional local AI hub between them. Hand-offs: Pacenotes and Debrief exchange stack traces and log checks, Pacenotes sends Sighter test plans and gets results, Sighter sends Debrief run bundles, Debrief and Pacenotes drive Sighter as MCP hosts (Debrief reproduces a bug from a video), Debrief uses Pitwall as its AI engine once paired (its built-in engine is the fallback), Sighter uses Pitwall as its vision model and agent planner, Pitcrew sends Debrief job logs and Dyno sends it issues (both lines pass beside Pitwall, not through it), Dyno sends installed software and machine health, Pitcrew runs CI for all, and Spotter will feed Sighter smoke tests later. Underneath, Paddock provides the kits (UI kit and design system, shared Rust crates, diagram kit, icon set, conformance checks, release practices, lessons) and two layers: the App shell every app uses (startup protection and safe mode, Report a problem, background services and login items, notifications and service health, dialogs, jobs and progress, settings, about and updates, the Storage page, undo, theme) and, on top of it, the Workbench for the IDE-style apps Debrief, Pacenotes and Sighter (docked panes with the layout planner, activity bar, Explorer, command palette, AI pane); Pitcrew, Pitwall, Spotter and Dyno use the shell with pages.
svg.text: Seven local-first tools for people who keep systems running
One private AI hub, one shared foundation. Each app is good alone and better together.
